issue.title: @Deprecated annotation added on a property
issue.body:
Im generating a class from list of property specs. The list has primitive and String elements filtered from the original class. 
Generated class is supposed to only have props from the list.

Original class:

```
@Serializable
data class Person(
    @SerialName("mName") val name: String,
    val surname: String?,
    val age: Int,
    val dog: Dog,
    val listOfDogs: List<Dog>,
    val listOfInts: List<Int>
)
```

Using metadata I successfully filtered properties and made them into a `List<PropertySpec>`. Im leaving the code for that too, in case it is useful to solve the issue. Otherwise, just skip next two blocks.

```
        val metadata = element.getAnnotation(Metadata::class.java)
        val typeSpec = metadata.toImmutableKmClass().toTypeSpec(
            ElementsClassInspector.create(processingEnv.elementUtils, processingEnv.typeUtils)
        )
        val membersSeparator = PropertyTypesSeparator(typeSpec)
        val primitives = membersSeparator.getPrimitiveProperties()
```

```
internal class PropertyTypesSeparator(private val classType: TypeSpec) {

    private val primitiveFields = mutableListOf<PropertySpec>()
    private val compositeFields = mutableListOf<PropertySpec>()

    init {
        processClassParameters()
    }

    fun getPrimitiveProperties(): List<PropertySpec> {
        return primitiveFields.toList()
    }

    fun getCompositeProperties(): List<PropertySpec> {
        return compositeFields.toList()
    }

    private fun processClassParameters() {
        classType.propertySpecs.forEach { property ->
            if (property.type is ParameterizedTypeName) {
                if ((property.type as ParameterizedTypeName).isCollection()) {
                    primitiveFields.add(property)
                } else {
                    compositeFields.add(property)
                }
            } else {
                if (property.type.isPrimitiveOrString()) {
                    primitiveFields.add(property)
                } else {
                    compositeFields.add(property)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private fun TypeName.isPrimitiveOrString(): Boolean {
        return when (this) {
            STRING,
            BOOLEAN,
            BYTE,
            SHORT,
            INT,
            LONG,
            CHAR,
            FLOAT,
            DOUBLE,
            CHAR_SEQUENCE,
            NUMBER,
            BOOLEAN_ARRAY,
            BYTE_ARRAY,
            SHORT_ARRAY,
            INT_ARRAY,
            LONG_ARRAY,
            CHAR_ARRAY,
            FLOAT_ARRAY,
            DOUBLE_ARRAY,
            U_BYTE,
            U_SHORT,
            U_INT,
            U_LONG,
            U_BYTE_ARRAY,
            U_SHORT_ARRAY,
            U_INT_ARRAY,
            U_LONG_ARRAY,
            STRING.copy(nullable = true),
            BOOLEAN.copy(nullable = true),
            BYTE.copy(nullable = true),
            SHORT.copy(nullable = true),
            INT.copy(nullable = true),
            LONG.copy(nullable = true),
            CHAR.copy(nullable = true),
            FLOAT.copy(nullable = true),
            DOUBLE.copy(nullable = true),
            CHAR_SEQUENCE.copy(nullable = true),
            NUMBER.copy(nullable = true),
            BOOLEAN_ARRAY.copy(nullable = true),
            BYTE_ARRAY.copy(nullable = true),
            SHORT_ARRAY.copy(nullable = true),
            INT_ARRAY.copy(nullable = true),
            LONG_ARRAY.copy(nullable = true),
            CHAR_ARRAY.copy(nullable = true),
            FLOAT_ARRAY.copy(nullable = true),
            DOUBLE_ARRAY.copy(nullable = true),
            U_BYTE.copy(nullable = true),
            U_SHORT.copy(nullable = true),
            U_INT.copy(nullable = true),
            U_LONG.copy(nullable = true),
            U_BYTE_ARRAY.copy(nullable = true),
            U_SHORT_ARRAY.copy(nullable = true),
            U_INT_ARRAY.copy(nullable = true),
            U_LONG_ARRAY.copy(nullable = true) -> true
            else -> false
        }
    }

    private fun ParameterizedTypeName.isCollection(): Boolean {

        return this.typeArguments.all { it.isPrimitiveOrString() } && when (rawType) {
            ARRAY,
            ITERABLE,
            COLLECTION,
            LIST,
            SET,
            MAP,
            MAP_ENTRY,
            MUTABLE_ITERABLE,
            MUTABLE_COLLECTION,
            MUTABLE_LIST,
            MUTABLE_SET,
            MUTABLE_MAP,
            MUTABLE_MAP_ENTRY,
            ARRAY.copy(nullable = true),
            ITERABLE.copy(nullable = true),
            COLLECTION.copy(nullable = true),
            LIST.copy(nullable = true),
            SET.copy(nullable = true),
            MAP.copy(nullable = true),
            MAP_ENTRY.copy(nullable = true),
            MUTABLE_ITERABLE.copy(nullable = true),
            MUTABLE_COLLECTION.copy(nullable = true),
            MUTABLE_LIST.copy(nullable = true),
            MUTABLE_SET.copy(nullable = true),
            MUTABLE_MAP.copy(nullable = true),
            MUTABLE_MAP_ENTRY.copy(nullable = true) -> true
            else -> false
        }
    }
}
```

This is code that I use for generation:

```
    fun build(
        attributes: List<PropertySpec>,
        packageName: String,
        className: String
    ): FileSpec {
        val parameterSpecs = attributes.map {
            ParameterSpec.builder(it.name, it.type).build()
        }

        return FileSpec.builder(packageName, className)

```

This is the output class that I get:

```
@Serializable

  public val age: Int,
```

issue.title: JavaPoet Interop
issue.body:
This is more of a question/feature suggestion. I'm working on a project where I'm using both JavaPoet and KotlinPoet (JavaPoet for some code and then Kotlin extensions that make the API sweeter for Kotlin users). 

One thing that I really wished for would be mapping between JavaPoet and KotlinPoet using extension functions. Possible use-cases would be to map between JavaPoet's `ClassName` and KotlinPoet's `ClassName` with something like `com.squareup.javapoet.ClassName.toKClassName()` which will give you the corresponding KotlinPoet `ClassName`. This would be similar for parameters, methods etc and give library developers a very easy path to write Kotlin extensions for their annotation processing libraries with minimal change to their existing codebase.

issue.title: Type name clash detection does not work if clashing type is only used as superclass
issue.body:
It was a bit hard to describe this accurately, so please have a look at this example:

```
import com.squareup.kotlinpoet.ClassName
import com.squareup.kotlinpoet.FileSpec
import com.squareup.kotlinpoet.FunSpec
import com.squareup.kotlinpoet.TypeSpec

val namespace = "test"

val kotlinExceptionName = ClassName("kotlin", "Exception")
val customExceptionName = ClassName(namespace, "Exception")
val customException = TypeSpec
        .classBuilder("Exception")
        .superclass(kotlinExceptionName)
        .addFunction(
                FunSpec
                        .builder("test")
                        .addParameter("e", customExceptionName)
                        .build()
        )
        .build()


FileSpec.builder(namespace, "a.kt")
        .addType(customException)
        .build()
        .toString()

val funn = FunSpec.builder("test")
        .addParameter("e", customExceptionName)
        .addParameter("f", kotlinExceptionName)
        .build()

FileSpec.builder(namespace, "b.kt")
        .addType(customException)
        .addFunction(funn)
        .build()
        .toString()
```

this outputs
```
package test

import kotlin.Exception

class Exception : Exception() {
  fun test(e: Exception) {
  }
}
```

and

```
package test

class Exception : kotlin.Exception() {
  fun test(e: Exception) {
  }
}

fun test(e: Exception, f: kotlin.Exception) {
}
```

So in the second case where the clashing names are also used as parameters, the disambiguation works correctly, even for the inheritance. But in the first case, where the superclass should also be fully qualified, it does not work.

issue.title: Support JvmName annotations in reflective metadata support
issue.body:
Right now - `@JvmName` annotations are recognized when using the elements-based API, but not with reflection since they're only `BINARY`-retained. We should be able to infer this fairly easily though - if the field or method signature names don't match the metadata name, infer and add the annotation with their names in it.

Tricky part will be trying to only do this for element handlers that require runtime retention for annotations. We could maybe add a `supportsNonRuntimeRetainedAnnotations` property to `ElementHandler` and, if that's `false`, do the custom inference. There are probably a couple of other annotations that would benefit from this that are being duplicated in the elements implementation right now (this is why they currently use `Set` 😓)

issue.body:

I was using this library to generate the following code

issue.title: Add FileFacade support in metadata
KSP interop outputs annotation's arrays incorrectly
issue.body:
Hey.

I'm in a process of migrating my project [hilt-binder](https://github.com/mars885/hilt-binder) to use the KSP interop artifact. However, I stubled upon the issue where if there is an annotation that has arrays as parameters, then the poet produces what seems to be invalid Kotlin code.

For example, in my project I have this [test](https://github.com/mars885/hilt-binder/blob/33870aed5b00da8a4ed7cc555daadd5a7c3e44a7/hilt-binder-compiler/src/test/java/com/paulrybitskyi/hiltbinder/processor/HiltBinderTest.kt#L3266), where the main input file is:
```kotlin
import com.paulrybitskyi.hiltbinder.BindType

@CustomQualifier(
    boolValue = true,
    byteValue = 10,
    charValue = ',',
    shortValue = Short.MAX_VALUE,
    intValue = -10,
    longValue = 100L,
    floatValue = -15F,
    doubleValue = 50.0,
    stringValue = "string",
    enumValue = CustomQualifierType.ONE,
    annotationValue = InnerAnno(
        intValue = 0,
        longValue = 500L,
        classValue = CustomQualifierClass::class
    ),
    classValue = CustomQualifierClass::class,
    boolArray = [true, false],
    byteArray = [100, 105],
    charArray = ['A', 'B', 'C'],
    shortArray = [Short.MIN_VALUE, Short.MAX_VALUE],
    intArray = [0, 10, 20],
    longArray = [10L, 20L, 30L],
    floatArray = [Float.MAX_VALUE, Float.MIN_VALUE],
    doubleArray = [100.0, 200.0, 300.0],
    stringArray = ["one", "two", "three"],
    enumArray = [
        CustomQualifierType.ONE,
        CustomQualifierType.TWO,
        CustomQualifierType.THREE
    ],
    annotationArray = [
        InnerAnno(
            intValue = 0,
            longValue = 1L,
            classValue = Test::class
        ),
        InnerAnno(
            intValue = 10,
            longValue = 100L,
            classValue = Testable::class
        )
    ],
    classArray = [
        Test::class,
        Testable::class,
        CustomQualifierClass::class
    ]
)
@BindType(withQualifier = true)
class Test : Testable
```
The correct output produced by using my own [utils](https://github.com/mars885/hilt-binder/blob/33870aed5b00da8a4ed7cc555daadd5a7c3e44a7/compiler-processing/src/main/java/com/paulrybitskyi/hiltbinder/compiler/processing/ksp/utils/PoetUtils.kt) to map from KSP types to KotlinPoet ones:

```kotlin
// Generated by @BindType. Do not modify!

import dagger.Binds
import dagger.Module
import dagger.hilt.InstallIn
import dagger.hilt.components.SingletonComponent

@Module
@InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class)
internal interface HiltBinder_SingletonComponentModule {
    @Binds
    @CustomQualifier(
        boolValue = true,
        byteValue = 10,
        charValue = ',',
        shortValue = 32767,
        intValue = -10,
        longValue = 100,
        floatValue = -15.0f,
        doubleValue = 50.0,
        stringValue = "string",
        enumValue = CustomQualifierType.ONE,
        annotationValue = InnerAnno(intValue = 0, longValue = 500, classValue =
            CustomQualifierClass::class),
        classValue = CustomQualifierClass::class,
        boolArray = [true, false],
        byteArray = [100, 105],
        charArray = ['A', 'B', 'C'],
        shortArray = [-32768, 32767],
        intArray = [0, 10, 20],
        longArray = [10, 20, 30],
        floatArray = [3.4028235E38f, 1.4E-45f],
        doubleArray = [100.0, 200.0, 300.0],
        stringArray = ["one", "two", "three"],
        enumArray = [CustomQualifierType.ONE, CustomQualifierType.TWO, CustomQualifierType.THREE],
        annotationArray = [InnerAnno(intValue = 0, longValue = 1, classValue = Test::class),
            InnerAnno(intValue = 10, longValue = 100, classValue = Testable::class)],
        classArray = [Test::class, Testable::class, CustomQualifierClass::class],
    )
    fun bind_Test(binding: Test): Testable
}
```
However, when using the KSP interop artifact now, the output is as follows:
```kotlin
@InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class)
internal interface HiltBinder_SingletonComponentModule {
    @CustomQualifier(
        boolValue = true,
        byteValue = 10,
        charValue = ',',
        shortValue = 32767.toShort(),
        intValue = -10,
        longValue = 100,
        floatValue = -15.0f,
        doubleValue = 50.0,
        stringValue = "string",
        enumValue = CustomQualifierType.ONE,
        annotationValue = InnerAnno(intValue = 0, longValue = 500, classValue =
            CustomQualifierClass::class),
        classValue = CustomQualifierClass::class,
        boolArray = arrayOf(true, false),
        byteArray = arrayOf(100, 105),
        charArray = arrayOf('A', 'B', 'C'),
        shortArray = arrayOf(-32768.toShort(), 32767.toShort()),
        intArray = arrayOf(0, 10, 20),
        longArray = arrayOf(10, 20, 30),
        floatArray = arrayOf(3.4028235E38f, 1.4E-45f),
        doubleArray = arrayOf(100.0, 200.0, 300.0),
        stringArray = arrayOf("one", "two", "three"),
        enumArray = arrayOf(CustomQualifierType.ONE, CustomQualifierType.TWO,
            CustomQualifierType.THREE),
        annotationArray = arrayOf(InnerAnno(intValue = 0, longValue = 1, classValue = Test::class),
            InnerAnno(intValue = 10, longValue = 100, classValue = Testable::class)),
        classArray = arrayOf(Test::class, Testable::class, CustomQualifierClass::class),
    )
    fun bind_Test(binding: Test): Testable
}
```
The output now is not compilable, because of type mismatches between expecting types like `ByteArray`, `IntArray`, but receiving `Array<Byte>`, `Array<Int>`.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14782808/183223981-31f76e3e-1669-417b-9d98-cc3bdd93f232.png)

The most straightforward solution I found is to replace `arrayOf` with literals `[]` [here](https://github.com/square/kotlinpoet/blob/d685eca08d6de064bdf16511be496bcd17e668ab/interop/ksp/src/main/kotlin/com/squareup/kotlinpoet/ksp/Annotations.kt#L74-L79).

issue.title: When calling a function that includes a space in the name, a new line is sometimes inserted in the middle of the function name.
Consider error-deprecated `ClassName(String)` overload
issue.body:
Sometimes I accidentally forget to split the simple name and write `ClassName("com.example.Foo")`. This fails at runtime.
```
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: simpleNames must not be empty
        at com.squareup.kotlinpoet.ClassName.<init>(TypeName.kt:323)
```

It would be nice if it failed at compile-time. This can be done with something like
```kotlin
@Deprecated("Simple names must not be empty", level = ERROR)
fun ClassName(value: String): Nothing = throw IAE(..)
```

issue.title: ElementHandler API
issue.body:
This is an issue to discuss any changes/tuning we should make to the `ElementHandler` API for metadata parsing.

Quick context: `ElementHandler` is a basic API for assisting kotlinpoet-metadata-specs APIs in fully describing the constructs around the code the metadata represents. There are pre-built reflective and `Elements`-based implementations right now.

The API has grown a little ad-hoc, so we should try to tease out where it can be better.

Current API:

```kotlin
/**
 * A basic interface for looking up information about JVM elements.
 */
@KotlinPoetMetadataPreview
interface ElementHandler {

  interface JvmModifier {
    fun annotationSpec(): AnnotationSpec
  }

  /** Modifiers that are annotations in Kotlin but modifier keywords in bytecode. */
  enum class JvmFieldModifier : JvmModifier {
    STATIC {
      override fun annotationSpec(): AnnotationSpec = AnnotationSpec.builder(JvmStatic::class.asClassName()).build()
    },
    TRANSIENT {
      override fun annotationSpec(): AnnotationSpec = AnnotationSpec.builder(Transient::class.asClassName()).build()
    },
    VOLATILE {
      override fun annotationSpec(): AnnotationSpec = AnnotationSpec.builder(Volatile::class.asClassName()).build()
    };
  }

  /** Modifiers that are annotations in Kotlin but modifier keywords in bytecode. */
  enum class JvmMethodModifier : JvmModifier {
    STATIC {
      override fun annotationSpec(): AnnotationSpec = AnnotationSpec.builder(JvmStatic::class.asClassName()).build()
    },
    SYNCHRONIZED {
      override fun annotationSpec(): AnnotationSpec = AnnotationSpec.builder(Synchronized::class.asClassName()).build()
    }
  }

  /**
   * Indicates if this element handler supports [AnnotationRetention.RUNTIME]-retained annotations.
   * This is used to indicate if manual inference of certain non-RUNTIME-retained annotations should
   * be done, such as [JvmName].
   */
  val supportsNonRuntimeRetainedAnnotations: Boolean

  /**
   * Looks up other classes, such as for nested members. Note that this class would always be
   * Kotlin, so Metadata can be relied on for this.
   *
   * @param jvmName The JVM name of the class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @return the read [ImmutableKmClass] from its metadata. If no class was found, this should throw
   *         an exception.
   */
  fun classFor(jvmName: String): ImmutableKmClass

  /**
   * Looks up a class and returns whether or not it is an interface. Note that this class can be
   * Java or Kotlin, so Metadata should not be relied on for this.
   *
   * @param jvmName The JVM name of the class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @return whether or not it is an interface.
   */
  fun isInterface(jvmName: String): Boolean

  /**
   * Looks up a given class field given its [JvmFieldSignature] and returns any [JvmModifier]s
   * found on it.
   *
   * @param classJvmName The JVM name of the class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @param fieldSignature The field to look up.
   * @param isJvmField Indicates if this field is a JvmField, in which case it should not be marked
   *                   as JvmStatic.
   * @return the set of found modifiers.
   */
  fun fieldJvmModifiers(
    classJvmName: String,
    fieldSignature: JvmFieldSignature,
    isJvmField: Boolean
  ): Set<JvmFieldModifier>

  /**
   * Looks up the annotations on a given class field given its [JvmFieldSignature].
   *
   * @param classJvmName The JVM name of the class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @param fieldSignature The field with annotations to look up.
   * @return the [AnnotationSpec] representations of the annotations on the target field.
   */
  fun fieldAnnotations(classJvmName: String, fieldSignature: JvmFieldSignature): List<AnnotationSpec>

  /**
   * Looks up a [JvmFieldSignature] and returns whether or not it is synthetic.
   *
   * @param classJvmName The JVM name of the class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @param fieldSignature The field to look up.
   * @return whether or not the field is synthetic.
   */
  fun isFieldSynthetic(classJvmName: String, fieldSignature: JvmFieldSignature): Boolean

  /**
   * Looks up a given class method given its [JvmMethodSignature] and returns any [JvmMethodModifier]s
   * found on it.
   *
   * @param classJvmName The JVM name of the class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @param methodSignature The method with annotations to look up.
   * @return the set of found modifiers.
   */
  fun methodJvmModifiers(classJvmName: String, methodSignature: JvmMethodSignature): Set<JvmMethodModifier>

  /**
   * Looks up the annotations on a given class constructor given its [JvmMethodSignature].
   *
   * @param classJvmName The JVM name of the class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @param constructorSignature The constructor with annotations to look up.
   * @return the [AnnotationSpec] representations of the annotations on the target method.
   */
  fun constructorAnnotations(classJvmName: String, constructorSignature: JvmMethodSignature): List<AnnotationSpec>

  /**
   * Looks up the annotations on a given class method given its [JvmMethodSignature].
   *
   * @param classJvmName The JVM name of the class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @param methodSignature The method with annotations to look up.
   * @return the [AnnotationSpec] representations of the annotations on the target method.
   */
  fun methodAnnotations(classJvmName: String, methodSignature: JvmMethodSignature): List<AnnotationSpec>

  /**
   * Looks up a [JvmMethodSignature] and returns whether or not it is synthetic.
   *
   * @param classJvmName The JVM name of the class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @param methodSignature The method to look up.
   * @return whether or not the method is synthetic.
   */
  fun isMethodSynthetic(classJvmName: String, methodSignature: JvmMethodSignature): Boolean

  /**
   * Looks up a given class method given its [JvmMethodSignature] and returns any thrown types
   * found on it. Used for [Throws][@Throws]
   *
   * @param classJvmName The JVM name of the class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @param methodSignature The method with annotations to look up.
   * @param isConstructor Indicates if [methodSignature] is a constructor.
   * @return the set of found thrown types, or empty.
   */
  fun methodExceptions(
    classJvmName: String,
    methodSignature: JvmMethodSignature,
    isConstructor: Boolean
  ): Set<TypeName>

  /**
   * Looks up the enum entry on a given enum given its member name.
   *
   * @param enumClassJvmName The JVM name of the enum class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @param memberName The simple member name.
   * @return the read [ImmutableKmClass] from its metadata, if any. For simple enum members with no
   *         class bodies, this should always be null.
   */
  fun enumEntry(enumClassJvmName: String, memberName: String): ImmutableKmClass?

  /**
   * Looks up the constant value on a given class field given its [JvmFieldSignature].
   *
   * @param classJvmName The JVM name of the class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @param fieldSignature The field with annotations to look up.
   * @return the [CodeBlock] representation of the constant on the target field. Null if the value
   *         cannot be resolved.
   */
  fun fieldConstant(classJvmName: String, fieldSignature: JvmFieldSignature): CodeBlock?

  /**
   * Looks up if a given [methodSignature] within [classJvmName] is an override of another method.
   * Implementers should search for a matching method signature in the supertypes/classes of
   * [classJvmName] to see if there are matches.
   *
   * @param classJvmName The JVM name of the class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @param methodSignature The method signature to check.
   * @return whether or not the method is an override.
   */
  fun isMethodOverride(classJvmName: String, methodSignature: JvmMethodSignature): Boolean

  /**
   * Looks up if a given [methodSignature] within [classJvmName] exists.
   *
   * @param classJvmName The JVM name of the class (example: `"org/foo/bar/Baz$Nested"`).
   * @param methodSignature The method signature to check.
   * @return whether or not the method exists.
   */
  fun methodExists(classJvmName: String, methodSignature: JvmMethodSignature): Boolean
}
```

Some added notes:
- `methodExists` is a means to check if a method is synthetic in enviornments that don't model synthetic constructs (such as elements). If a method is in metadata but not Elements, it's presumed synthetic.

issue.title: Support callable references
issue.body:
I frequently get tripped up generating function references due to a combination of the syntax required and how KotlinPoet handles imports.

For example, say I would like to generate a reference to the `Taco` constructor:

```kotlin
import com.example.Taco

val tacoFactory: () -> Taco = ::Taco
```

In KotlinPoet, I would try this, and it produces the expected output:

```kotlin

val TACO = ClassName("com.example", "Taco")

val file = FileSpec.builder("", "Taco.kt")
    .addProperty(
        PropertySpec.builder("tacoFactory", LambdaTypeName.get(null, emptyList(), TACO))
            .initializer("::%T", TACO)
            .build()
    )
    .build()
```

However, if Taco is a nested class, this doesn't work, because the syntax requires the `::` to come *after* the enclosing type. Replacing `TACO` above with `ClassName("com.example", "Food", "Taco")`:


```kotlin
import com.example.Food

val tacoFactory: () -> Food.Taco = ::Food.Taco      // This should be Food::Taco
```

To get this to work in the general case (e.g. for any `ClassName`, nested or not) requires a bunch of boilerplate that could be handled by KotlinPoet itself.

```kotlin
fun ClassName.constructorReference(): CodeBlock {
    val enclosingClassName = enclosingClassName()
    return if (enclosingClassName != null) {
        CodeBlock.of("%T::%L", enclosingClassName, simpleName)
    } else {
        CodeBlock.of("::%T", this)
    }
}
```

Of course, the `else` case isn't semantically correct, as it only works when KotlinPoet is able to import the type and use it without the qualifying package. I'm not sure how the above code could be modified to automatically import the non-nested type if I only use it in a constructor reference.

In addition to constructor references, there are also function and property references, which are syntactically similar to `MemberName`, but with the reference operator required before the member name in both qualified and unqualified usages. These are similarly difficult to generate if they are top-level members, as KotlinPoet wants to both emit the name and handle the import.

issue.title: Auto-suggested import aliases
issue.body:
This feature proposal stems from #924, where in case if a type cannot be imported due to a simple name clash, generating a reference to that type's constructor would produce broken code:

```kotlin
val squareTaco = ClassName("com.squareup.tacos", "Taco")
val twitterTaco = ClassName("com.twitter.tacos", "Taco")
val file = FileSpec.builder("com.squareup.example", "Tacos")
    .addFunction(FunSpec.builder("main")
        .addStatement("val squareTacosCreator = %L", squareTaco.constructorReference())
        .addStatement("val twitterTacosCreator = %L", twitterTaco.constructorReference())
        .build())
    .build()
println(file)

// Output:
//
// ...
// val squareTacosCreator = ::Taco
// val twitterTacosCreator = ::com.twitter.tacos.Taco // Fails to compile!
// ...
```

A similar problem occurs whenever a `MemberName` that cannot be imported due to a name clash is used as an extension function:

```kotlin
val kotlinIsNullOrEmpty = MemberName("kotlin.text", "isNullOrEmpty")
val cashIsNullOrEmpty = MemberName("com.squareup.cash.util", "isNullOrEmpty")
val file = FileSpec.builder("com.squareup.example", "Tacos")
    .addFunction(FunSpec.builder("main")
        .addStatement("println(%S.%M())", "Taco", kotlinIsNullOrEmpty)
        .addStatement("println(%S.%M())", "Taco", cashIsNullOrEmpty)
        .build())
    .build()
println(file)

// Output:
//
// ...
// println("Taco".isNullOrEmpty())
// println("Taco".com.squareup.cash.util.isNullOrEmpty())  // Fails to compile!
// ...
```

The workaround for this issue is to use [`FileSpec.Builder.addAliasedImport()`](https://square.github.io/kotlinpoet/1.x/kotlinpoet/com.squareup.kotlinpoet/-file-spec/-builder/add-aliased-import/). For instance, in the first example, `addAliasedImport(twitterTaco, "TwitterTaco")` will turn the output into:

```kotlin
...
val squareTacosCreator = ::Taco
val twitterTacosCreator = ::TwitterTaco
...
```

However, managing import aliases by hand is not ideal:

- First of all, this is not an intuitive solution to the problem. If valid import aliases are not provided KotlinPoet will silently generate broken code and we'll get bug reports.
- If the generated code changes, proposed import aliases may start clashing with newly introduced type names, which will again fail silently.
- If the simple name clash disappears due to changes in the generated code, proposed import aliases will become unnecessary, and there will be no clear indication that they can be removed.

### Proposal

- Update `CodeWriter` to keep track of types and members that could not be imported due to a name clash.
- For those types and members, generate unique aliases and use them to create `Import` instances.
- At the end of the import collection pass, `FileSpec` should retrieve the `Import`s from the `CodeWriter` and pass them into the new instance of `CodeWriter`, along with the `memberImports`.
- During the second pass, `CodeWriter` should treat generated import aliases in the same way as if they were added manually via `addAliasedImport()`.

#### Alias generation

Since import aliases are local to the generated file and will not be seen by the consumers of the API defined in this file, we should prefer correctness over readability, still making an effort to generate meaningful aliases. For types, we can prefix simple names with capitalized letters of each of the package name segments, e.g.:

```
com.squareup.cash.Taco -> CSCTaco
```

For members, we can use the same letters in lowercase and capitalize the first letter of the member name, e.g.:

```
com.squareup.cash.util.isNullOrEmpty -> cscuIsNullOrEmpty
```

The algorithm should be implemented by the `AliasAllocator`, which would function similarly to `NameAllocator`, holding on to the global pool of allocated aliases to avoid clashes. `AliasAllocator` can be made public and used as a utility when generating a valid alias is required outside of KotlinPoet. Having `AliasAllocator` would also allow us to introduce overloads to methods such as [`FileSpec.Builder.addAliasedImport()`](https://square.github.io/kotlinpoet/1.x/kotlinpoet/com.squareup.kotlinpoet/-file-spec/-builder/add-aliased-import/) or [`TypeAlias.builder()`](https://square.github.io/kotlinpoet/1.x/kotlinpoet/com.squareup.kotlinpoet/-type-alias-spec/builder/) which do not require passing the actual alias.

Looking for feedback on this feature and volunteers to build it.

issue.title: Improve name escaping logic

As demonstrated by #698, we incorrectly assume that any characters escaped by backticks form a correct name. This is not true, e.g. this will not compile:

We should fix name validation logic and throw if the name contains characters that can't be escaped.

issue.title: Come up with a better artifact layout
issue.body:
Libraries that process annotations and parse Kotlin metadata represent only a subset of KotlinPoet consumers, whereas other consumers, such as SQLDelight and Wire, have other types of input. Therefore, helpers for Metadata and Elements processing should be moved out of the main artifact, which should help keep it small and generic.

- Move recently introduced helpers for working with Kotlin metadata into a new artifact that depends on both `kotlinpoet` and `kotlinpoet-km`. **Milestone**: 1.4.
- Find good names for `kotlinpoet-km` and the new artifact. **Milestone**: 1.4.
- Move helpers for processing Elements into a new artifact. **Milestone**: 2.0.

issue.title: KSP interop outputs annotation parameter value of type `Char` incorrectly
issue.body:
Hey.

I'm in a process of migrating my project [hilt-binder](https://github.com/mars885/hilt-binder) to use the KSP interop artifact. However, I stubled upon the issue where if there is an annotation that has `Char` parameter, then the output code will be invalid because of the lack of the single quotes `'`.

For example:
`kotlinpoet/interop/ksp/test-processor/src/main/kotlin/com/squareup/kotlinpoet/ksp/test/processor/exampleAnnotations.kt`
```kotlin
package com.squareup.kotlinpoet.ksp.test.processor

import kotlin.reflect.KClass

annotation class ExampleAnnotation

annotation class ComprehensiveAnnotation<T : CharSequence>(
  // ...
  val char: Char, // <---------------- new type
  // ...
```
`kotlinpoet/interop/ksp/test-processor/src/test/kotlin/com/squareup/kotlinpoet/ksp/test/processor/TestProcessorTest.kt`
```kotlin
  @Test
  fun smokeTest() {
    val compilation = prepareCompilation(
      kotlin(
        "Example.kt",
        """
           package test

           import com.squareup.kotlinpoet.ksp.test.processor.AnnotationEnumValue
           import com.squareup.kotlinpoet.ksp.test.processor.AnotherAnnotation
           import com.squareup.kotlinpoet.ksp.test.processor.ComprehensiveAnnotation
           import com.squareup.kotlinpoet.ksp.test.processor.ExampleAnnotation

           typealias TypeAliasName = String
           typealias GenericTypeAlias = List<String>
           typealias ParameterizedTypeAlias<T> = List<T>
           
           // Input File
           @ComprehensiveAnnotation<String>(
             true, // Omit the name intentionally here to test names are still picked up
             booleanArray = [true],
             byte = 0.toByte(),
             byteArray = [0.toByte()],
             char = 'a', // <---------------- new type
             // ...

            // Output file
            assertThat(generatedFileText).isEqualTo(
              """
              package test
        
              // lots of imports
        
              @ComprehensiveAnnotation<String>(
                boolean = true,
                booleanArray = arrayOf(true),
                byte = 0.toByte(),
                byteArray = arrayOf(0.toByte()),
                char = a.toByte(), // <---------------- outputs a.toByte(), but should 'a'
                short = 0.toShort(),
```
I've forked a repo and provided a demo of the bug on the branch [bug_showcase_invalid_char_type_output](https://github.com/mars885/kotlinpoet/tree/bug_showcase_invalid_char_type_output).

Having checked your sources for a possible fix, it appears that [this line](https://github.com/square/kotlinpoet/blob/d685eca08d6de064bdf16511be496bcd17e668ab/interop/ksp/src/main/kotlin/com/squareup/kotlinpoet/ksp/Annotations.kt#L114)
`is Char -> CodeBlock.of("$value.toChar()")` should be made like this: `is Char -> CodeBlock.of("'%L'", value)`. I've tried that in a fork and it has successfully fixed the issue.

Would love to contribute if possible.
